at danse.explanation: "At danse" means "to dance": Vil du danse? (Do you want to dance?). To say who with, use med (with): Jeg danser med Anna (I dance with Anna).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **danse** til musikken.
sentence.en: I want to dance to the music.

at date.explanation: "At date" means "to date", to go out with someone to get to know them: Jeg dater en fra Aarhus (I am dating someone from Aarhus). For the day on a calendar, use en dato (a date on the calendar).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **date** en sød fyr.
sentence.en: She would like to date a nice guy.

at dele.explanation: "At dele" means "to share" and also "to divide". In math, it means divide: ti delt med to (ten divided by two).

sentence.da: Vi vil **dele** en pizza.
sentence.en: We want to share a pizza.

at dele ud.explanation: "At dele ud" means "to hand out", giving things to several people: Læreren deler papirer ud (The teacher hands out papers). Plain at dele means "to share": Vi deler en pizza (We share a pizza).

sentence.da: Han skal **dele ud** til alle børnene.
sentence.en: He is going to hand things out to all the children.

at deltage.explanation: "At deltage" means "to participate" or "to take part", and you add i (in) before the event: Jeg deltager i mødet (I am taking part in the meeting). It fits games and contests too: De deltager i konkurrencen (They are taking part in the competition).

sentence.da: Alle kan **deltage** i kurset gratis.
sentence.en: Everyone can take part in the course for free.

at designe.explanation: "At designe" means "to design": Hun designer smykker (She designs jewelry). Han designede en ny stol (He designed a new chair).

sentence.da: Min søster elsker at **designe** tøj.
sentence.en: My sister loves to design clothes.

at diskutere.explanation: "At diskutere" means "to discuss": Vi diskuterer planen (We are discussing the plan). For an angry fight, use at skændes (to quarrel): De skændes hele tiden (They quarrel all the time).

sentence.da: Vi skal **diskutere** problemet med læreren.
sentence.en: We have to discuss the problem with the teacher.

at dividere.explanation: "At dividere" means "to divide" in math: Jeg dividerer ti med to (I divide ten by two). To share something between people, say at dele (to share).

sentence.da: Du skal **dividere** tolv med tre.
sentence.en: You have to divide twelve by three.

at downloade.explanation: "At downloade" means "to download", to copy something from the internet onto your own device: Jeg downloader appen (I download the app).

sentence.da: Du kan **downloade** appen gratis.
sentence.en: You can download the app for free.

at dreje.explanation: "At dreje" means "to turn": Drej til højre (Turn right). It also works for turning a thing: Jeg drejer håndtaget (I turn the handle). Det drejer sig om penge (It is about money).

sentence.da: Du skal **dreje** til venstre ved banken.
sentence.en: You have to turn left at the bank.

at drikke.explanation: "At drikke" means "to drink", for water, coffee, beer and so on: Jeg drikker kaffe (I drink coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **drikke** et glas vand.
sentence.en: I want to drink a glass of water.

at drille.explanation: "At drille" means "to tease", usually in a playful way: Han driller sin lillesøster (He teases his little sister). Hurtful teasing is more like at mobbe (to bully).

sentence.da: Min bror elsker at **drille** mig.
sentence.en: My brother loves to tease me.

at droppe.explanation: "At droppe" means "to drop" a plan or "to skip" something: Jeg dropper festen (I am skipping the party). Vi droppede planen (We dropped the plan). It is casual talk.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **droppe** sukker i min kaffe.
sentence.en: I want to skip sugar in my coffee.

at drukne.explanation: "At drukne" means "to drown": Manden druknede i søen (The man drowned in the lake). You can also warn someone: Pas på, ellers drukner du! (Careful, or you will drown!)

sentence.da: Man kan **drukne** i dybt vand.
sentence.en: You can drown in deep water.

at dræbe.explanation: "At dræbe" means "to kill": Katten dræbte musen (The cat killed the mouse). To say someone was killed, use blev dræbt: Han blev dræbt (He was killed).

sentence.da: Ræven kan **dræbe** en høne.
sentence.en: The fox can kill a hen.

at drømme.explanation: "At drømme" means "to dream", both asleep and awake, and it takes om (about): Jeg drømte om dig (I dreamed about you). Hun drømmer om et stort hus (She dreams of a big house).

sentence.da: Jeg vil sove og **drømme** hele natten.
sentence.en: I want to sleep and dream all night.

at dufte.explanation: "At dufte" means "to smell nice": Blomsterne dufter dejligt (The flowers smell lovely). Plain at lugte (to smell) can also be bad: Det lugter af fisk (It smells like fish).

sentence.da: Det plejer at **dufte** dejligt her.
sentence.en: It usually smells lovely here.

at dukke op.explanation: "At dukke op" means "to show up", often when someone arrives or something appears unexpectedly: Han dukkede op klokken otte (He showed up at eight o'clock). On a screen it means "to pop up": En besked dukker op (A message pops up).

sentence.da: Jeg håber, at han vil **dukke op** i aften.
sentence.en: I hope that he will show up tonight.

at dumpe.explanation: "At dumpe" means "to fail (an exam)": Han dumpede til eksamen (He failed the exam). The opposite is at bestå (to pass): Hun bestod eksamen (She passed the exam).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **dumpe** til eksamen.
sentence.en: I don't want to fail the exam.

at dykke.explanation: "At dykke" means "to dive" under water: Børnene dykker efter sten (The children dive for stones). To dive in headfirst from a board, say at stupe (to dive in): Han stuper fra vippen (He dives from the board).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **dykke** og se fiskene i havet.
sentence.en: I would like to dive and see the fish in the sea.

at dyrke.explanation: "At dyrke" means "to grow" plants on purpose: Vi dyrker tomater (We grow tomatoes). It also means "to practice" a sport or hobby: Jeg dyrker yoga (I do yoga).

sentence.da: Min mor vil **dyrke** grøntsager i haven.
sentence.en: My mother wants to grow vegetables in the garden.

at dyrke sport.explanation: "At dyrke sport" means "to do sports" as a regular activity: Jeg dyrker sport hver uge (I do sports every week). For one sport, Danes often use at spille: Jeg spiller tennis (I play tennis).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **dyrke sport** mere i år.
sentence.en: I want to do more sports this year.

at dække.explanation: "At dække" means "to cover": Jeg dækker bordet med en dug (I cover the table with a cloth). It also works for costs: Forsikringen dækker skaden (The insurance covers the damage).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **dække** barnet med et tæppe.
sentence.en: I want to cover the child with a blanket.

at dække bord.explanation: "At dække bord" means "to set the table", putting the plates out before a meal: Kan du dække bord? (Can you set the table?)

sentence.da: Kan du **dække bord**, mens jeg laver mad?
sentence.en: Can you set the table while I cook?

at dø.explanation: "At dø" means "to die". For "have died" Danish uses er (am / is), not har (have): Han er død (He has died).

sentence.da: Planter kan **dø** uden vand.
sentence.en: Plants can die without water.

da.explanation: "Da" means "when", for something that happened once in the past. Compare Da jeg kom hjem, sov børnene (When I came home, the children were asleep) with Når jeg kommer hjem, sover børnene (When I get home, the children are asleep: now or later, not in the past).

sentence.da: **Da** jeg kom hjem, sov børnene.
sentence.en: When I came home, the children were asleep.

dagen efter.explanation: "Dagen efter" means "the day after" something: Dagen efter festen var jeg træt (The day after the party I was tired). On its own, the next day is næste dag.

forms.en: The day after, he came home

sentence.da: Jeg var træt **dagen efter** festen.
sentence.en: I was tired the day after the party.

dagens ret.explanation: "Dagens ret" means "dish of the day". Word for word, it is the day's dish: dagens (the day's) and ret (dish).

sentence.da: **Dagens ret** er fisk og kartofler.
sentence.en: The dish of the day is fish and potatoes.

daglig.explanation: "Daglig" means "daily" and describes what happens every day: den daglige rutine (the daily routine). To say something happens every day, use hver dag: Jeg løber hver dag (I run every day).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **daglig** avis.
sentence.en: I read a daily newspaper.

dagligdags.explanation: "Dagligdags" means "everyday" and describes ordinary things that happen all the time: et dagligdags problem (an everyday problem). It also fits language: dagligdags sprog (everyday language).

sentence.da: Det er et **dagligdags** ord i Danmark.
sentence.en: It is an everyday word in Denmark.

dagligt.explanation: "Dagligt" means "daily" or "every day": Jeg drikker kaffe dagligt (I drink coffee daily). Before an en-word, use daglig instead.

sentence.da: Han træner **dagligt** og spiser sundt.
sentence.en: He trains daily and eats healthily.

dagligvarer.explanation: "Dagligvarer" means "groceries": everyday goods like food and household things. It is built from daglig (daily) and varer (goods) and is always plural.

sentence.da: Jeg køber **dagligvarer** i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: I buy groceries at the supermarket.

damp.explanation: "Damp" means "steam", the hot cloud from boiling water: Der kommer damp fra gryden (Steam is coming from the pot). It also fogs up mirrors and windows.

forms.en: There is steam in the bathroom.

sentence.da: Der kommer **damp** op fra kaffen.
sentence.en: Steam is rising from the coffee.

dansk.explanation: "Dansk" means "Danish", the language and also things from Denmark. As a school subject, it is used without en or et: Jeg har dansk (I have Danish class). Language names start with a small letter: dansk (Danish), engelsk (English).

sentence.da: Jeg bor i Danmark og taler **dansk**.
sentence.en: I live in Denmark and speak Danish.

data.explanation: "Data" means "data", facts and numbers collected for a purpose: Vi samler data fra mange mennesker (We collect data from many people).

sentence.da: Vi bruger **data** fra mange mennesker.
sentence.en: We use data from many people.

davs.explanation: "Davs" means "hi", a short, casual greeting for people you know. Hej (hi) is the everyday greeting that suits everyone.

sentence.da: **Davs**, Peter! Hvordan går det?
sentence.en: Hi, Peter! How is it going?

de.explanation: "De" means "they". Compare De ser mig (They see me) with Jeg ser dem (I see them), where dem means "them". De is also "the" before many things: de store huse (the big houses).

sentence.da: Anna og Lars? **De** er hjemme.
sentence.en: Anna and Lars? They are at home.

december.explanation: "December" means "December". Danish writes month names with a small letter, so you write i december (in December), not i December.

sentence.da: Vi fejrer jul i **december**.
sentence.en: We celebrate Christmas in December.

defekt.explanation: "Defekt" means "defective", for a machine or part that does not work as it should: Printeren er defekt (The printer is defective). In everyday speech, ødelagt (broken) is also common.

sentence.da: Vaskemaskinen er **defekt**, og den vil ikke starte.
sentence.en: The washing machine is defective, and it will not start.

dejlig.explanation: "Dejlig" means "lovely" or "nice": Dejligt! means "Lovely!" and Det er dejligt vejr means "It is lovely weather".

sentence.da: I dag er det en **dejlig** dag.
sentence.en: Today it is a lovely day.

dem.explanation: "Dem" means "them". Compare De ser mig (They see me) with Jeg ser dem (I see them): de (they) is for the ones doing it, dem for the ones it happens to.

sentence.da: Mine naboer er søde. Jeg kender **dem**.
sentence.en: My neighbors are nice. I know them.

den.explanation: "Den" means "it" for words that take en. Compare Jeg har en bil. Den er rød (I have a car. It is red) with Jeg har et hus. Det er rødt (I have a house. It is red). Den also means "the" before a describing word: den store bil (the big car).

sentence.da: Se på bilen! **Den** er meget stor.
sentence.en: Look at the car! It is very big.

dengang.explanation: "Dengang" means "back then" and always points to the past: Dengang var vi unge (Back then we were young). Jeg kendte hende dengang (I knew her back then).

forms.en: What were you doing back then?
My father lived here back then.

sentence.da: **Dengang** boede vi i Odense og var glade.
sentence.en: Back then we lived in Odense and were happy.

denne.explanation: "Denne" means "this" with words that take en. Compare denne bil (this car) with dette hus (this house, as hus takes et). It sounds formal; in everyday speech people say den her bil (this car).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **denne** bil.
sentence.en: I want this car.

dens.explanation: "Dens" means "its" and belongs to something that is an en-word: Bilen er gammel, og dens motor er stor (The car is old, and its engine is big). Things that are et-words use a different word.

sentence.da: Bilen er gammel, men **dens** motor er stærk.
sentence.en: The car is old, but its engine is strong.

der.explanation: "Der" means "there". Compare Han er her (He is here) with Han er der (He is there). At the start of a sentence, it says something exists: Der er mange børn (There are many children). It can also mean "who": manden, der bor her (the man who lives here).

sentence.da: **Der** er en kat i haven.
sentence.en: There is a cat in the garden.

derefter.explanation: "Derefter" means "after that". Compare efter maden (after the meal) with derefter (after that): Vi ser en film, og derefter går vi i seng (We watch a film, and after that we go to bed).

sentence.da: Først mad, og **derefter** kaffe.
sentence.en: First food, and after that coffee.

deres.explanation: "Deres" means "their". Compare Det er hans hus (It is his house) with Det er deres hus (It is their house). It stays the same for one thing or many: deres hund (their dog), deres hunde (their dogs).

sentence.da: Anna og Bo bor i **deres** hus.
sentence.en: Anna and Bo live in their house.

derfor.explanation: "Derfor" means "that is why". The same fact can be said two ways: Jeg er syg, derfor bliver jeg hjemme (I am sick, that is why I am staying home) and Jeg bliver hjemme, fordi jeg er syg (I am staying home because I am sick).

forms.en: that is why I am here

sentence.da: Det regner. **Derfor** er jeg hjemme.
sentence.en: It is raining. That is why I am home.

derfra.explanation: "Derfra" means "from there". Compare Jeg kommer herfra (I come from here) with Jeg kommer derfra (I come from there).

forms.en: What can you see from there?

sentence.da: Banken er der. Jeg kommer **derfra**.
sentence.en: The bank is there. I come from there.

derhen.explanation: "Derhen" means "(to) there" and is used when you move toward a place: Vi tager bussen derhen (We take the bus there). To say where someone is, use der (there): Han er der (He is there).

sentence.da: Hvordan kommer jeg **derhen**?
sentence.en: How do I get there?

derhjemme.explanation: "Derhjemme" means "at home", said about your home when you are not in it or about life there in general: Derhjemme har vi to katte (At home we have two cats). Compare Jeg er hjemme (I am at home, right now).

forms.en: what do you do at home?

sentence.da: **Derhjemme** taler vi dansk.
sentence.en: At home we speak Danish.

derinde.explanation: "Derinde" means "in there". Compare Jeg er herinde (I am in here) with Katten er derinde (The cat is in there).

forms.en: in there in the living room

sentence.da: Min mor er **derinde** i stuen.
sentence.en: My mother is in there in the living room.

dermed.explanation: "Dermed" means "thereby" and "with that", linking a result to what was just said: Han vandt, og dermed fik han guldet (He won, and with that he got the gold). In casual talk, så (so) is more common.

sentence.da: Vi har betalt, og **dermed** er sagen afgjort.
sentence.en: We have paid, and with that the matter is settled.

dernede.explanation: "Dernede" means "down there". Compare Katten er deroppe (The cat is up there) with Katten er dernede (The cat is down there).

sentence.da: Bilen står **dernede** i kælderen.
sentence.en: The car is down there in the basement.

deroppe.explanation: "Deroppe" means "up there" and tells where something is when it is higher than you: Se, der er en fugl deroppe (Look, there is a bird up there).

forms.en: The cat is sitting up there

sentence.da: Kan du se fuglen **deroppe** i træet?
sentence.en: Can you see the bird up there in the tree?

derovre.explanation: "Derovre" means "over there", for a place at a distance that you can point to: Bogen ligger derovre (The book is over there). To move there, use derover: Jeg går derover (I am going over there).

sentence.da: Min bil står **derovre** ved huset.
sentence.en: My car is parked over there by the house.

derude.explanation: "Derude" means "out there". Compare Børnene er derinde (The children are in there) with Børnene er derude (The children are out there).

sentence.da: Se ud af vinduet! Børnene leger **derude**.
sentence.en: Look out of the window! The children are playing out there.

design.explanation: "Design" means "design" and covers how something looks, like a chair, a phone or a website: Det er et flot design (It is a nice design).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide det enkle **design**.
sentence.en: I like the simple design.

desperat.explanation: "Desperat" means "desperate", for a person who sees no way out or for what they do: Han gjorde et desperat forsøg (He made a desperate attempt). Hun er desperat efter et job (She is desperate for a job).

sentence.da: Han var **desperat** og ringede til alle.
sentence.en: He was desperate and called everyone.

desuden.explanation: "Desuden" means "furthermore" and "besides" and adds one more point: Maden er god, og desuden er den billig (The food is good, and besides, it is cheap).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, og **desuden** er det sent.
sentence.en: I am tired, and besides, it is late.

desværre.explanation: "Desværre" means "unfortunately". Use it before bad news or a no: Desværre kan jeg ikke komme (Unfortunately, I can't come). It sounds softer and more polite than just Nej (No).

sentence.da: **Desværre** har jeg ikke tid i dag.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, I do not have time today.

det.explanation: "Det" means "it" or "that". Use it for a thing that takes et: Jeg har et hus, og det er stort (I have a house, and it is big). Things that take en use den: Jeg har en bil, og den er stor (I have a car, and it is big). Det is also used for weather and general statements: Det regner (It is raining), Det er sjovt (That is fun).

forms.en: I know it / I know that.

sentence.da: Se på huset! **Det** er meget gammelt.
sentence.en: Look at the house! It is very old.

det er.explanation: "Det er" means "it is" or "that is"; Danish uses the same two words for both. Use it to name things or describe them: Det er sent (It is late).

sentence.da: **Det er** en god dag i dag.
sentence.en: It is a good day today.

det er en god idé.explanation: "Det er en god idé" means "that's a good idea", said to agree with a suggestion. You can shorten it to God idé! (Good idea!).

sentence.da: Café i dag? **Det er en god idé.**
sentence.en: Cafe today? That's a good idea.

det er fint med mig.explanation: "Det er fint med mig" means "that's fine with me" and agrees to a plan: Skal vi mødes klokken fem? (Shall we meet at five?) Det er fint med mig. Change mig to dig to ask: Er det fint med dig? (Is that fine with you?).

forms.da: Ja, det er fint med mig.
Hvis det er fint med dig.

sentence.da: Vi kan mødes klokken fem, **det er fint med mig**.
sentence.en: We can meet at five, that's fine with me.

det er i orden.explanation: "Det er i orden" means "it's okay" or "that's fine". Danes say it in reply to undskyld (sorry) and to agree to a plan. I orden literally means "in order". Ask er det i orden? (is that okay?) to check if something suits the other person.

sentence.da: Undskyld! — **Det er i orden.**
sentence.en: Sorry! — It's okay.

det er ikke så svært.explanation: "Det er ikke så svært" means "it's not that hard". Svært means "difficult" and "ikke så" means "not so".

sentence.da: Dansk? **Det er ikke så svært.**
sentence.en: Danish? It's not that hard.

det er lige det.explanation: "Det er lige det" means "that's exactly it" and you say it when someone has hit the right point: Du er bare træt? Ja, det er lige det (You are just tired? Yes, that's exactly it). Lige det alone means "exactly that": Jeg ville have lige det (I wanted exactly that).

forms.da: Det er lige det, jeg mener
Nej, det er ikke lige det

sentence.da: Præcis, **det er lige det**, jeg mener.
sentence.en: Exactly, that's just what I mean.

det er lige meget.explanation: "Det er lige meget" means "it doesn't matter". Use it when you are happy with any choice. Careful with tone: Det er mig lige meget (I don't care) can sound rude, so say det gør ikke noget (it's no problem) when you want to be kind.

forms.da: Det er lige meget, hvad du vælger.
forms.en: It doesn't matter what you choose.

sentence.da: Te eller kaffe? **Det er lige meget.**
sentence.en: Tea or coffee? It doesn't matter.

det er min skyld.explanation: "Det er min skyld" means "it's my fault" and takes the blame: Undskyld, det er min skyld (Sorry, it's my fault). Change min to hans (his) to blame someone else: Det er hans skyld (It's his fault).

sentence.da: Jeg glemte at ringe, **det er min skyld**.
sentence.en: I forgot to call, it's my fault.

det er rigtigt.explanation: "Det er rigtigt" means "that's right", said to agree that something is correct or true. Be careful: rigtig also means "really" before another word, as in rigtig godt (really good). A short alternative is ja, præcis (yes, exactly).

sentence.da: Du bor i Aarhus? **Det er rigtigt.**
sentence.en: You live in Aarhus? That's right.

det er synd.explanation: "Det er synd" means "that's a shame" or "that's too bad", and shows sympathy when something goes wrong. To say you feel sorry for someone, add for and the person: Det er synd for ham (I feel sorry for him).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke komme? **Det er synd!**
sentence.en: You can't come? That's a shame!

det giver ikke mening.explanation: "Det giver ikke mening" means "that doesn't make sense": Din plan giver ikke mening (Your plan doesn't make sense). For something you cannot follow, you can also say Jeg forstår det ikke (I don't understand).

forms.en: That makes no sense at all

sentence.da: Du siger ja og nej, og **det giver ikke mening**.
sentence.en: You say yes and no, and that doesn't make sense.

det giver mening.explanation: "Det giver mening" means "that makes sense": Nu giver det mening (Now it makes sense). The word mening (meaning, sense) also means "opinion": Hvad er din mening? (What is your opinion?).

sentence.da: Nu forstår jeg, og **det giver mening**.
sentence.en: Now I understand, and that makes sense.

det går fint.explanation: "Det går fint" means "it's going fine" and is a common answer to Hvordan går det? (How is it going?). Swap fint (fine) for godt (well) or dårligt (badly) to change the mood.

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? **Det går fint.**
sentence.en: How is it going? It's going fine.

det går godt.explanation: "Det går godt" means "it's going well" and is a standard answer to Hvordan går det? (How's it going?). After answering, it is polite to ask og dig? (and you?).

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? **Det går godt.**
sentence.en: How is it going? It's going well.

det gør ikke noget.explanation: "Det gør ikke noget" means "it's okay" or "no problem", what you say when someone says Undskyld (Sorry). Word for word, it says it does not do anything. Do not mix it up with det er lige meget (it doesn't matter), which is for choices.

forms.da: Det gør ikke noget, jeg venter.

sentence.da: "Undskyld!" – "**Det gør ikke noget.**"
sentence.en: "Sorry!" – "It's okay."

det håber jeg.explanation: "Det håber jeg" means "I hope so", a short reply to a question about something that might happen. To say "I hope not", add ikke (not) at the end: Det håber jeg ikke.

sentence.da: Bliver det godt vejr? **Det håber jeg.**
sentence.en: Will the weather be good? I hope so.

det kan godt være.explanation: "Det kan godt være" means "that may be" and admits something could be true, often before you disagree: Det kan godt være, men jeg tvivler (That may be, but I doubt it).

forms.da: Det kan godt være, du har ret.
forms.en: That may be, you could be right.

sentence.da: **Det kan godt være**, men jeg ser det anderledes.
sentence.en: That may be, but I see it differently.

det kan man ikke vide.explanation: "Det kan man ikke vide" means "you never know" and is said when the future is uncertain: Måske vinder vi. Det kan man ikke vide (Maybe we will win. You never know). Literally it says that one cannot know it.

sentence.da: Måske bliver det godt. **Det kan man ikke vide**.
sentence.en: Maybe it will be good. You never know.

det kommer an på.explanation: "Det kommer an på" means "it depends": Kommer du? Det kommer an på vejret (Are you coming? It depends on the weather). It always ends with på (on) and then what it depends on.

sentence.da: **Det kommer an på** hvor meget det koster.
sentence.en: It depends on how much it costs.

det lyder godt.explanation: "Det lyder godt" means "that sounds good". Use it to react positively to a plan, an offer or an idea. At lyde means "to sound". Put rigtig (really) before godt (good) to sound more enthusiastic: Det lyder rigtig godt.

sentence.da: Middag klokken seks? **Det lyder godt.**
sentence.en: Dinner at six? That sounds good.

det passer.explanation: "Det passer" means "that's true" and confirms a fact: Du bor i Aarhus, ikke? (You live in Aarhus, right?) Det passer. Add ikke to say the opposite: Det passer ikke (That's not true).

sentence.da: Du er fra Norge, ikke? Ja, **det passer**.
sentence.en: You are from Norway, right? Yes, that's true.

det passer ikke.explanation: "Det passer ikke" means "that's not true" and corrects a wrong claim: Du ringede aldrig! (You never called!) Det passer ikke, jeg ringede i går (That's not true, I called yesterday). Without ikke it says the claim is true.

sentence.da: **Det passer ikke**, jeg var der ikke i går.
sentence.en: That's not true, I wasn't there yesterday.

det tror jeg.explanation: "Det tror jeg" means "I think so" or "I believe so", a polite, slightly unsure reply when you aren't completely certain. Add ikke (not) to say "I don't think so": Det tror jeg ikke.

sentence.da: Er han hjemme? **Det tror jeg.**
sentence.en: Is he home? I think so.

det tror jeg ikke.explanation: "Det tror jeg ikke" means "I don't think so", a soft way to say no. Word for word, it is that think I not. It sounds gentler than a plain nej (no).

sentence.da: Regner det i dag? **Det tror jeg ikke.**
sentence.en: Is it raining today? I don't think so.

det var dog utroligt.explanation: "Det var dog utroligt" means "that's incredible" and reacts to surprising news. The little word dog (though) adds surprise: Han vandt tre gange! Det var dog utroligt! (He won three times! That's incredible!).

sentence.da: Hun vandt tre gange i træk, **det var dog utroligt**!
sentence.en: She won three times in a row, that's incredible!

det var så lidt.explanation: "Det var så lidt" means "you're welcome" or "don't mention it". Word for word, it says it was so little, as if the favor was nothing. It is a warm, slightly informal answer to tak (thanks).

forms.da: Tak for hjælpen! – Det var så lidt.
forms.en: Thanks for the help! – Don't mention it.

sentence.da: Tak for hjælpen! **Det var så lidt.**
sentence.en: Thanks for the help! Don't mention it.

det ved jeg ikke.explanation: "Det ved jeg ikke" means "I don't know". Det (that) comes first, then ved jeg (know I). At vide (to know) is for facts; for knowing a person or place use at kende (to know).

forms.da: Det ved jeg ikke noget om.

sentence.da: Hvor er Peter? **Det ved jeg ikke.**
sentence.en: Where is Peter? I don't know.

det vil sige.explanation: "Det vil sige" means "that is to say" and is used before you explain or sum up: Jeg bor i Jylland, det vil sige i Aarhus (I live in Jutland, that is to say in Aarhus). In writing it is often shortened to dvs.

forms.da: Det vil sige, at du kommer
forms.en: That is to say, you are coming

sentence.da: Vi mødes klokken otte, **det vil sige** om en time.
sentence.en: We meet at eight, that is to say in an hour.

dets.explanation: "Dets" means "its" and belongs to something that is an et-word: Æblet er rødt, og dets smag er sød (The apple is red and its taste is sweet). Things that are en-words use a different word.

sentence.da: Huset er gammelt, men **dets** tag er nyt.
sentence.en: The house is old, but its roof is new.

dette.explanation: "Dette" means "this" with a word that takes et: dette hus (this house). With a word that takes en, use denne: denne bil (this car). It sounds a bit formal; in everyday speech Danes say det her: Jeg vil have det her (I want this one).

sentence.da: Jeg vil købe **dette** hus.
sentence.en: I want to buy this house.

diarré.explanation: "Diarré" means "diarrhea": Barnet har diarré (The child has diarrhea). It often comes with mavesyge (a stomach bug).

sentence.da: Jeg har **diarré** og skal blive hjemme.
sentence.en: I have diarrhea and have to stay home.

diesel.explanation: "Diesel" means "diesel", a fuel used by many vans and trucks: Bilen kører på diesel (The car runs on diesel). Do not mix it up with benzin (gasoline).

sentence.da: Varebilen kører på **diesel**, ikke på benzin.
sentence.en: The van runs on diesel, not on gasoline.

dig.explanation: "Dig" means "you" when something is done to you: Jeg elsker dig (I love you). Du is the one who does it: Du elsker mig (You love me). It is also used after little words like med (with): Jeg kommer med dig (I am coming with you). It is for one person; for several people say jer (you, many).

sentence.da: Jeg kan høre **dig**.
sentence.en: I can hear you.

digital.explanation: "Digital" means "digital". It looks like the English word, but the stress is on the last part: di-gi-TAL.

sentence.da: Klokken har kun tal. Den er **digital**.
sentence.en: The clock has only numbers. It is digital.

dild.explanation: "Dild" means "dill", a green herb that goes well with fish: Laks med dild (Salmon with dill). It is also used on new potatoes: Nye kartofler med dild (New potatoes with dill).

sentence.da: Fisken smager godt med **dild**.
sentence.en: The fish tastes good with dill.

din.explanation: "Din" means "your" or "yours" when you talk to one person and the thing takes en: din bil (your car). For a thing that takes et, it is dit: dit hus (your house). For more than one thing, it is dine: dine sko (your shoes).

sentence.da: Her er **din** kaffe.
sentence.en: Here is your coffee.

dine.explanation: "Dine" means "your" or "yours" when there is more than one thing: dine sko (your shoes). For one thing, it is din or "dit": din sko (your shoe), dit hus (your house). It is also used on its own: Skoene er dine (The shoes are yours).

sentence.da: Tag **dine** sko på.
sentence.en: Put your shoes on.

direkte.explanation: "Direkte" means "directly" and also "direct": Gå direkte til lægen (Go straight to the doctor). A direct train or flight has no stops on the way: et direkte tog (a direct train).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **direkte** hjem efter arbejde.
sentence.en: I go straight home after work.

disse.explanation: "Disse" means "these": disse sko (these shoes). For one thing, it is denne or "dette": denne sko (this shoe), dette hus (this house). It sounds a bit formal; in everyday speech, Danes say de her: de her sko (these shoes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **disse** sko.
sentence.en: I like these shoes.

dit.explanation: "Dit" means "your" or "yours" when you talk to one person and the thing takes et: dit hus (your house), dit navn (your name). For a thing that takes en, it is din: din bil (your car). For more than one thing, it is dine: dine sko (your shoes).

sentence.da: Hvad er **dit** navn?
sentence.en: What is your name?

dobbelt.explanation: "Dobbelt" means "double" and "twice as much": Jeg tog en dobbelt espresso (I took a double espresso). It starts many words, such as dobbeltværelse (double room).

sentence.da: Det koster **dobbelt** så meget i byen.
sentence.en: It costs twice as much in the city.

dog.explanation: "Dog" means "though", "still" or "anyway". It adds a little contrast: Det er dyrt, men jeg køber det dog (It is expensive, but I am buying it anyway). In a command, it makes the request friendlier: Kom dog ind! (Do come in!). It is not the same as men (but): Han er sød, men sur (He is sweet but grumpy).

sentence.da: Kom **dog** ind, Peter!
sentence.en: Do come in, Peter!

doven.explanation: "Doven" means "lazy" and describes someone who avoids work: Han er for doven til at rydde op (He is too lazy to clean up). The opposite is flittig (diligent).

sentence.da: Han er **doven** og ligger i sofaen hele dagen.
sentence.en: He is lazy and lies on the sofa all day.

dressing.explanation: "En dressing" means "a dressing", the cold sauce you put on a salad: Vil du have dressing på salaten? (Do you want dressing on the salad?) A warm sauce with meat is en sovs (a sauce) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg laver en **dressing** til salaten.
sentence.en: I make a dressing for the salad.

drikkepenge.explanation: "Drikkepenge" means "a tip", the extra money you give for good service. It is used without en or et: Tak, behold resten som drikkepenge (Thanks, keep the change as a tip).

sentence.da: Vi gav tjeneren **drikkepenge**, fordi maden var god.
sentence.en: We gave the waiter a tip because the food was good.

drikkevarer.explanation: "Drikkevarer" means "drinks" or "beverages" as a group, like on a menu or in a shop: Mad og drikkevarer (Food and drinks). For one single drink, say en drik: en kold drik (a cold drink).

sentence.da: Vi sælger mad og **drikkevarer** i kiosken.
sentence.en: We sell food and drinks in the kiosk.

du.explanation: "Du" means "you" when you talk to one person: Du er sød (You are sweet). Danes use it with almost everyone, even older people and your boss. When something is done to you, it is dig: Jeg ser dig (I see you). When you talk to several people, say I: I er søde (You are all sweet).

sentence.da: Hvor bor **du**?
sentence.en: Where do you live?

dum.explanation: "Dum" means "stupid" or "silly". Said about a person, it can sound rude: Du er dum (You are stupid). About things, it is milder: Det var dumt (That was silly).

sentence.da: Det var en **dum** fejl.
sentence.en: That was a stupid mistake.

dyb.explanation: "Dyb" means "deep", as in deep water or a deep hole. It also works for sleep and voices: en dyb søvn (a deep sleep), en dyb stemme (a deep voice).

sentence.da: Søen er for **dyb** til børn.
sentence.en: The lake is too deep for children.

dygtig.explanation: "Dygtig" means "skilled" or "capable", good at what you do: Hun er dygtig til sprog (She is good at languages). Dygtig! is also a way to say "Well done!"

sentence.da: Han er **dygtig** og lærer hurtigt.
sentence.en: He is capable and learns quickly.

dyr.explanation: "Dyr" means "expensive", as in Det er for dyrt (It is too expensive). Be careful: et dyr is also a word of its own meaning "an animal".

sentence.da: Jakken koster 5000 kroner. Den er meget **dyr**.
sentence.en: The jacket costs 5000 kroner. It is very expensive.

dårlig.explanation: "Dårlig" means "bad", and it also means "unwell": Jeg har det dårligt means "I feel bad" or "I feel ill". The words for "worse" and "worst" are different: værre (worse) and værst (worst).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og har en **dårlig** dag.
sentence.en: I am sick and having a bad day.

dårlig til.explanation: "Dårlig til" means "bad at": Jeg er dårlig til matematik (I am bad at math). Before an action, add at: dårlig til at tegne (bad at drawing).

forms.da: Jeg er dårlig til at lave mad.
Vi er dårlige til at danse.

sentence.da: Han er **dårlig til** at svømme, men han prøver.
sentence.en: He is bad at swimming, but he tries.

død.explanation: "Død" means "dead", for people, animals and plants. It is also used for things that have stopped working: Min telefon er død (My phone is dead).

sentence.da: Blomsten er **død** uden vand.
sentence.en: The flower is dead without water.

en dag.explanation: "En dag" means "a day", as in hver dag (every day) and god dag (hello, good day). The days of the week end in -dag, for example mandag (Monday) and tirsdag (Tuesday).

sentence.da: Mandag er den første **dag** i ugen.
sentence.en: Monday is the first day of the week.

en dagbog.explanation: "En dagbog" means "a diary", a book where you write about your own days: Min dagbog er privat (My diary is private). It is built from dag (day) and bog (book).

sentence.da: Hun skriver hver aften i sin **dagbog**.
sentence.en: She writes in her diary every evening.

en dagsrejse.explanation: "En dagsrejse" means "a day trip", a trip you start and finish in one day: Det er en lang dagsrejse til Jylland (It is a long day trip to Jutland).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en **dagsrejse** og er hjemme i aften.
sentence.en: We go on a day trip and are home tonight.

en dal.explanation: "En dal" means "a valley", low land between hills or mountains: Landsbyen ligger i en grøn dal (The village lies in a green valley). Floden løber gennem dalen (The river runs through the valley).

sentence.da: Floden løber gennem en smuk **dal**.
sentence.en: The river runs through a beautiful valley.

en dam.explanation: "En dam" means "a pond", a small body of still water: Der svømmer ænder i dammen (Ducks swim in the pond). A bigger one is en sø (a lake).

sentence.da: Der bor mange frøer i den lille **dam**.
sentence.en: Many frogs live in the little pond.

en dame.explanation: "En dame" means "a lady", a polite word for a woman. You often see Damer on a restroom door, meaning the women's restroom. Mine damer og herrer means "Ladies and gentlemen".

sentence.da: Den **dame** i kjole er min tante.
sentence.en: The lady in the dress is my aunt.

en dans.explanation: "En dans" means "a dance": Vi lærer en ny dans (We are learning a new dance). The action is at danse (to dance): Jeg danser hver weekend (I dance every weekend).

sentence.da: Jeg har lært en ny **dans** til festen.
sentence.en: I have learned a new dance for the party.

en danser.explanation: "En danser" means "a dancer", a person who dances, for fun or as a job: Hun er danser i et teater (She is a dancer in a theater).

sentence.da: Hun er en god **danser**, og hun øver hver dag.
sentence.en: She is a good dancer, and she practices every day.

en dansker.explanation: "En dansker" means "a Dane", a person from Denmark. The word is the same for men and women. To say what nationality someone is, Danish leaves out en: Han er dansker means "He is a Dane".

sentence.da: Han bor i Danmark og er **dansker**.
sentence.en: He lives in Denmark and is a Dane.

en database.explanation: "En database" means "a database", a place where a company or a program keeps lots of information: Banken har en database med alle kunder (The bank has a database with all its customers).

sentence.da: Vi gemmer alle navne i en **database**.
sentence.en: We save all the names in a database.

en date.explanation: "En date" means "a date", a romantic meeting between two people: Jeg har en date i aften (I have a date tonight). It is not a date on the calendar. That is en dato (a date).

sentence.da: Han har en **date** i aften og er meget nervøs.
sentence.en: He has a date tonight and is very nervous.

en dato.explanation: "En dato" means "a date" on the calendar, such as 5 March. Use it to ask: Hvad er datoen i dag? (What is the date today?). Do not mix it up with a romantic date, which is en date (borrowed from English).

sentence.da: Hvilken **dato** er det i dag?
sentence.en: What date is it today?

en datter.explanation: "En datter" means "a daughter". Hvor gammel er din datter? means "How old is your daughter?".

sentence.da: Jeg har en søn og en **datter**.
sentence.en: I have a son and a daughter.

en deadline.explanation: "En deadline" means "a deadline": Deadlinen er snart (The deadline is soon). Danish also has en frist (a time limit).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **deadline** på fredag.
sentence.en: I have a deadline on Friday.

en deciliter.explanation: "En deciliter" means "a deciliter", one tenth of a liter, often used in recipes: Opskriften bruger fem deciliter mælk (The recipe uses five deciliters of milk). After a number, it stays deciliter.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger to **deciliter** mel i brødet.
sentence.en: I use two deciliters of flour in the bread.

en definition.explanation: "En definition" means "a definition", an exact explanation of what a word means: Hvad er definitionen på frihed? (What is the definition of freedom?). The word after på says which word is being defined.

sentence.da: Jeg kender ikke ordets **definition**.
sentence.en: I do not know the definition of the word.

en dej.explanation: "En dej" means "a dough", and also "a batter", the soft mix you make before baking: Dejen skal hæve (The dough has to rise).

sentence.da: Jeg laver **dej** af mel og vand.
sentence.en: I make dough from flour and water.

en dekoration.explanation: "En dekoration" means "a decoration", something that makes a room or a table look nicer: Der er flotte dekorationer i stuen (There are beautiful decorations in the living room). The action is at dekorere (to decorate).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **dekoration** til bordet.
sentence.en: I am buying a decoration for the table.

en del.explanation: "En del" means "a part": Det er en del af planen (It is part of the plan). It also means "quite a lot": Der er en del mennesker her (There are quite a few people here).

sentence.da: Musik er en stor **del** af mit liv.
sentence.en: Music is a big part of my life.

en delfin.explanation: "En delfin" means "a dolphin", a smart sea animal that jumps out of the water: Delfinen hopper højt (The dolphin jumps high). Delfiner svømmer ofte i store grupper (Dolphins often swim in big groups).

sentence.da: Jeg så en **delfin** hoppe op af vandet.
sentence.en: I saw a dolphin jump out of the water.

en deltager.explanation: "En deltager" means "a participant", someone who takes part in something. It comes from at deltage (to take part): Der er tyve deltagere på kurset (There are twenty participants on the course).

sentence.da: Hver **deltager** får en lille gave.
sentence.en: Each participant gets a small gift.

en deltagerliste.explanation: "En deltagerliste" means "a list of participants". It is built from en deltager (a participant) and en liste (a list): Er jeg på deltagerlisten? (Am I on the participant list?).

sentence.da: Der er tyve navne på vores **deltagerliste**.
sentence.en: There are twenty names on our participant list.

en deodorant.explanation: "En deodorant" means "a deodorant": Jeg bruger deodorant hver morgen (I use deodorant every morning).

sentence.da: Jeg lugter ikke, fordi jeg bruger **deodorant**.
sentence.en: I do not smell because I use deodorant.

en designer.explanation: "En designer" means "a designer", someone who plans how things look, such as clothes, furniture or websites: Hun er designer (She is a designer).

sentence.da: Hun er **designer** og laver smukt tøj.
sentence.en: She is a designer and makes beautiful clothes.

en dessert.explanation: "En dessert" means "a dessert", the sweet dish at the end of a meal. It is spelled like the English word, but the stress is at the end: des-SERT.

sentence.da: Efter maden vil jeg have en **dessert**.
sentence.en: After the meal I want a dessert.

en destination.explanation: "En destination" means "a destination", the place a trip is going to: Min destination er Rom (My destination is Rome).

sentence.da: Vores **destination** er en lille by ved havet.
sentence.en: Our destination is a small town by the sea.

en detalje.explanation: "En detalje" means "a detail", a small part of something bigger: Jeg husker ikke detaljerne (I don't remember the details). Hun forklarede alt i detaljer (She explained everything in detail).

sentence.da: Billedet er flot, men én **detalje** er forkert.
sentence.en: The picture is nice, but one detail is wrong.

en detektiv.explanation: "En detektiv" means "a detective", a person who finds out who did a crime: Detektiven løste sagen (The detective solved the case). It can be a police officer or a private person.

sentence.da: Den kloge **detektiv** fandt hurtigt ud af sandheden.
sentence.en: The clever detective quickly found out the truth.

en direktør.explanation: "En direktør" means "a director" or "a CEO", the person who runs a whole company: Direktøren har et møde (The director has a meeting). A person who guides a smaller team is en leder (a leader).

sentence.da: Min **direktør** har et møde i dag.
sentence.en: My director has a meeting today.

en diskussion.explanation: "En diskussion" means "a discussion": Der var en lang diskussion om politik (There was a long discussion about politics). It can be heated: Det blev en heftig diskussion (It became a heated discussion).

sentence.da: Vi havde en **diskussion** om, hvem der skulle betale.
sentence.en: We had a discussion about who should pay.

en doktor.explanation: "En doktor" means "a doctor", but in everyday Danish people mostly say en læge (a medical doctor). Still, Jeg skal til doktoren (I am going to the doctor) is fine in casual speech.

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og skal til **doktor** Hansen.
sentence.en: I am sick and going to Doctor Hansen.

en dokumentar.explanation: "En dokumentar" means "a documentary", a film about real events or real people: Vi så en dokumentar om dyr (We watched a documentary about animals). It is not a made-up story.

sentence.da: Vi så en **dokumentar** om havet i går.
sentence.en: We watched a documentary about the sea yesterday.

en dollar.explanation: "En dollar" means "a dollar". Hvad koster det i dollar? means "What does it cost in dollars?".

sentence.da: Det koster ti **dollar**.
sentence.en: It costs ten dollars.

en dommer.explanation: "En dommer" means "a judge", the person who decides a case in court: Dommeren siger, at han er skyldig (The judge says he is guilty). In sports it also means "a referee": Dommeren blæste i fløjten (The referee blew the whistle).

sentence.da: I retten bestemmer en **dommer** straffen.
sentence.en: In court, a judge decides the punishment.

en donut.explanation: "En donut" means "a donut", the round fried ring with a hole in the middle, often with icing: Jeg tager en donut med glasur (I'll have a donut with icing).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **donut** med chokolade.
sentence.en: I would like a donut with chocolate.

en drage.explanation: "En drage" means "a dragon", and also "a kite" you fly in the wind: Dragen spyr ild (The dragon breathes fire). Jeg har en rød drage (I have a red kite).

sentence.da: Børnene flyver med en **drage** på stranden.
sentence.en: The kids fly a kite on the beach.

en dreng.explanation: "En dreng" means "a boy", a young male child. For a young adult, say en ung mand (a young man).

sentence.da: Den lille **dreng** leger med sin bil.
sentence.en: The little boy plays with his car.

en drik.explanation: "En drik" means "a drink", from at drikke (to drink). In everyday speech, people usually name the drink itself, like en kaffe (a coffee) or en øl (a beer).

sentence.da: Må jeg få en kold **drik**?
sentence.en: May I have a cold drink?

en drink.explanation: "En drink" means "a drink", but only a mixed one like a cocktail: Vil du have en drink? (Would you like a cocktail?) For any other drink, say noget at drikke (something to drink).

sentence.da: Hun bestiller en **drink** i baren.
sentence.en: She orders a cocktail at the bar.

en dronning.explanation: "En dronning" means "a queen": Dronningen bor i et slot (The queen lives in a castle). It can be the ruler or the wife of a king.

sentence.da: Landets **dronning** vinkede til folk fra altanen.
sentence.en: The country's queen waved to people from the balcony.

en drøm.explanation: "En drøm" means "a dream", both while you sleep and as a wish: Jeg havde en mærkelig drøm i nat (I had a strange dream last night). Hendes drøm er at rejse jorden rundt (Her dream is to travel around the world).

sentence.da: Min **drøm** er at bo ved havet.
sentence.en: My dream is to live by the sea.

en due.explanation: "En due" means "a pigeon" and also "a dove": Der sidder duer på pladsen (Pigeons sit on the square). A white dove as a symbol of peace is en fredsdue (a peace dove).

sentence.da: Der sidder en **due** på taget.
sentence.en: A pigeon sits on the roof.

en duft.explanation: "En duft" means "a scent" or "a fragrance", usually a pleasant smell: Jeg kan lide duften af brød (I like the scent of bread). For a bad smell, say lugt (smell): Der er dårlig lugt her (There is a bad smell here).

sentence.da: Der er en dejlig **duft** af kaffe i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a lovely scent of coffee in the kitchen.

en dug.explanation: "En dug" means "a tablecloth": Hun skifter dugen før middagen (She changes the tablecloth before dinner). It also means "dew", the water on grass in the morning.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en hvid **dug** på bordet.
sentence.en: I put a white tablecloth on the table.

en dukke.explanation: "En dukke" means "a doll", a toy for children. A puppet in a show is also "en dukke", and "dukketeater" means "puppet theater".

sentence.da: Pigen leger med sin **dukke**.
sentence.en: The girl is playing with her doll.

en dybde.explanation: "En dybde" means "a depth", how far down something goes: Dybden er to meter (The depth is two meters). For how far up something goes, use en højde (a height).

sentence.da: Søen har en **dybde** på ti meter.
sentence.en: The lake has a depth of ten meters.

en dyne.explanation: "En dyne" means "a duvet", the thick filled cover on a bed: Jeg sover under en varm dyne (I sleep under a warm duvet). A tæppe (rug / blanket) is more often for the sofa or the floor.

sentence.da: Om vinteren sover jeg under en tyk **dyne**.
sentence.en: In winter I sleep under a thick duvet.

en dyreven.explanation: "En dyreven" means "an animal lover". It is built from dyr (animal) and ven (friend), so it literally says "animal friend". Hun er en stor dyreven (She is a big animal lover).

sentence.da: Min onkel er en stor **dyreven** og har fem katte.
sentence.en: My uncle is a big animal lover and has five cats.

en dyrlæge.explanation: "En dyrlæge" means "a veterinarian". It is built from dyr (animal) and læge (doctor): Hun er dyrlæge og behandler heste (She is a vet and treats horses).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til en **dyrlæge**, fordi min hund er syg.
sentence.en: I am calling a vet because my dog is sick.

en dåse.explanation: "En dåse" means "a can" made of metal: en dåse tomater (a can of tomatoes). For a glass jar, use et glas (a jar): et glas marmelade (a jar of jam).

sentence.da: Jeg åbner en **dåse** tomater til sovsen.
sentence.en: I open a can of tomatoes for the sauce.

en dåseåbner.explanation: "En dåseåbner" means "a can opener": Hvor er dåseåbneren? (Where is the can opener?) It is built from dåse (can) and åbner (opener).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne dåsen uden en **dåseåbner**.
sentence.en: I cannot open the can without a can opener.

en dør.explanation: "En dør" means "a door". Common phrases are at åbne døren (to open the door) and at lukke døren (to close the door). The letter ø sounds a bit like the u in fur.

sentence.da: Jeg åbner en **dør** og går ind.
sentence.en: I open a door and go in.

en dørkarm.explanation: "En dørkarm" means "a door frame". It is dør (door) plus karm (frame): Jeg maler dørkarmen hvid (I am painting the door frame white).

sentence.da: Han slår hovedet i den lave **dørkarm**.
sentence.en: He hits his head on the low door frame.

en dørklokke.explanation: "En dørklokke" means "a doorbell". It is built from dør (door) and klokke (bell): Jeg ringer på dørklokken (I ring the doorbell).

sentence.da: Vi har en ny **dørklokke**, og den er meget høj.
sentence.en: We have a new doorbell, and it is very loud.

en dørmåtte.explanation: "En dørmåtte" means "a doormat", the mat you wipe your shoes on: Tør fødderne på dørmåtten (Wipe your feet on the doormat).

sentence.da: Der ligger en **dørmåtte** foran vores dør.
sentence.en: There is a doormat in front of our door.

et dankort.explanation: "Et dankort" means "a Dankort", the Danish debit card. To ask if a store takes it, say Kan jeg betale med dankort? (Can I pay by Dankort?). Note that Danish leaves out the word a after med here.

sentence.da: Jeg betaler i butikken med **dankort**.
sentence.en: I pay at the store with a Dankort.

et danskkursus.explanation: "Et danskkursus" means "a Danish course", built from dansk (Danish) and kursus (course): Jeg tager et danskkursus (I am taking a Danish course).

sentence.da: Hun har **danskkursus** om aftenen.
sentence.en: She has Danish class in the evening.

et decimaltal.explanation: "Et decimaltal" means "a decimal number", a number with digits after the comma. Danes write a comma where English uses a point: 2,5 (2.5).

sentence.da: Tallet 3,5 er et **decimaltal**.
sentence.en: The number 3.5 is a decimal number.

et depositum.explanation: "Et depositum" means "a deposit", money you pay when you rent a home and get back when you move out, if nothing is damaged: Depositummet er 15.000 kroner (The deposit is 15,000 kroner).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler et **depositum**, når jeg flytter ind.
sentence.en: I pay a deposit when I move in.

et diagram.explanation: "Et diagram" means "a chart" or "a diagram", a picture that shows numbers or how something works: Diagrammet viser, hvor mange der kom (The chart shows how many came).

sentence.da: Læreren viser et **diagram** med søjler og tal.
sentence.en: The teacher shows a chart with columns and numbers.

et digt.explanation: "Et digt" means "a poem", a short text with lines that often rhyme: Jeg skriver et digt til min mor (I am writing a poem for my mother). The person who writes it is en digter (a poet).

sentence.da: Hun læser et smukt **digt** højt for klassen.
sentence.en: She reads a beautiful poem aloud to the class.

et dobbeltværelse.explanation: "Et dobbeltværelse" means "a double room", a hotel room for two people. It is made of dobbelt (double) and et værelse (a room).

sentence.da: Vi to vil gerne have et **dobbeltværelse**.
sentence.en: The two of us would like a double room.

et dokument.explanation: "Et dokument" means "a document", either a paper or a file on a computer: Jeg printer dokumentet (I am printing the document). It can also be an official paper: Husk at tage dokumentet med (Remember to bring the document).

sentence.da: Jeg skal skrive under på et **dokument**.
sentence.en: I have to sign a document.

et download.explanation: "Et download" means "a download", a file you copy from the internet to your device. The action is at downloade (to download): Jeg downloader en app (I am downloading an app).

sentence.da: Dit **download** er færdigt, og filen ligger på skrivebordet.
sentence.en: Your download is finished, and the file is on the desktop.

et drivhus.explanation: "Et drivhus" means "a greenhouse", a glass building where plants grow warm and fast: Vi har agurker i drivhuset (We have cucumbers in the greenhouse).

sentence.da: Tomaterne vokser hurtigt i et varmt **drivhus**.
sentence.en: The tomatoes grow fast in a warm greenhouse.

et drømmejob.explanation: "Et drømmejob" means "a dream job", the work you would most like to have: Det er mit drømmejob (It is my dream job). It is built from en drøm (a dream) and et job (a job).

sentence.da: Endelig har jeg fået mit **drømmejob** som kok.
sentence.en: I have finally gotten my dream job as a cook.

et dynebetræk.explanation: "Et dynebetræk" means "a duvet cover". It is built from dyne (duvet) and betræk (cover): Jeg vasker dynebetrækket (I wash the duvet cover).

sentence.da: Jeg har købt et nyt **dynebetræk** til sengen.
sentence.en: I have bought a new duvet cover for the bed.

et dyr.explanation: "Et dyr" means "an animal". Et vildt dyr means "a wild animal".

sentence.da: Hunde og katte er **dyr**.
sentence.en: Dogs and cats are animals.

et dæk.explanation: "Et dæk" means "a tire" on a car or bike: Jeg skal have nye dæk til bilen (I need new tires for the car). It also means "a deck" on a ship: Skibet har tre dæk (The ship has three decks).

sentence.da: Bilen har et fladt **dæk**.
sentence.en: The car has a flat tire.

et døgn.explanation: "Et døgn" means "a day", but the full 24 hours, day and night: Butikken er åben hele døgnet (The store is open all day and night). A normal en dag can mean only the daytime.

sentence.da: Der er fireogtyve timer i et **døgn**.
sentence.en: There are twenty-four hours in a day.

et dørslag.explanation: "Et dørslag" means "a colander", a bowl with holes for draining pasta and vegetables: Kartoflerne skal i dørslaget (The potatoes go in the colander).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder pastaen i et **dørslag**.
sentence.en: I pour the pasta into a colander.
